paper.title: Cascading Bandits for Large-Scale Recommendation Problems

unmapped: Attraction probability of each item is linear in known item features: w(e) = x_e^T theta*, with theta* unknown and shared across items
Ground set of L items (canonical K); list of K items (canonical m) recommended; reward = 1 - prod(1 - w(a_k)), items attract independently
settings.definition_quote: we assume that the attraction probability of each item $e$, $\bar{w}(e)$, can be approximated by a linear combination of some known $d$-dimensional feature vector $x_e$ and an unknown $d$-dimensional parameter vector of $\theta^\ast$ ... We first derive a regret bound on CascadeLinUCB, under the assumptions that (1) $\bar{w}(e) = x_e^T \theta^\ast$ for all $e \in E$ and (2) $\| x_e \|_2 \leq 1$ for all $e \in E$.

symbols.sigma_alg: algorithm parameter sigma > 0 controlling the learning rate (Gram matrix M_t = sigma^-2 X^T X + I)
symbols.m: paper's K: number of recommended items in the list
symbols.K: paper's L: number of items in the ground set (not appearing in bound)

conditions: w(e) = x_e^T theta* for all items (perfect linear generalization)
optimal list unique as a set
tuning: c >= (1/sigma) sqrt(d log(1 + nK/(d sigma^2)) + 2 log(nK)) + ||theta*||_2

source.label: thm:bound
source.quote: Under the above assumptions, for any $\sigma > 0$ and any $c \geq \frac{1}{\sigma} \sqrt{d \log ( 1 + \frac{nK}{d \sigma^2} )+ 2 \log ( nK ) } + \|\theta^*\|_2$, if we run CascadeLinUCB with parameters $\sigma$ and $c$, then $R(n) \leq 2c K \sqrt{\frac{dn \log [1+ \frac{nK}{d\sigma^2}]}{\log ( 1 + \frac{1}{\sigma^2} )} }+ 1.$

results.notes: Regret defined as expected f(A*,w_t)-f(A_t,w_t) with fixed A*, equivalent to pseudo-regret. Paper's n=T, K=m (list length), L=ground set size. With sigma=1 and c=sqrt(d log(1+nK/d)+2log(nK))+eta, eta>=||theta*||, paper remarks R(n)=O~(K d sqrt(n)) (in canonical: O~(m d sqrt(T))). Bound independent of L.
